native_mechanisms: A single rolling sphere is the sole carried memory folded across the whole ordered pile of marks (one streaming accumulator, no backward references).
Each mark is pressed into the sphere, then a fixed count of tumbles down the trail mixes it in before the next mark is taken (fixed round count per input chunk).
Only the final hairline crack in the last stalk is kept as the token; all intermediate faces, dust and footprints are swept away (output derived solely from final state).
One wrong mark reshapes the entire sphere, not a sliver — every downstream stalk cracks differently (full-state avalanche from any single input bit).
The next carry is read as the angle of a crack — bending/spinning, never scaling (add-rotate-xor mixing, no multiplication).
core_technique: Off-the-shelf SipHash-1-3-style ARX accumulator (4x64-bit state, fixed rounds per 8-byte word, length-padded tail, 4 finalisation rounds, XOR-folded output) with a generic AVX2 4-lane shift/or/add block path as a speed optimisation.
